macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: Wall Street ends mixed as Fed signals further rate hikes
items.summary: The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 1.11% to 50,198.17 and the S&P 500 declined 0.23% to 7,323.64, while the Nasdaq Composite rose 0.42% to 24,429.89. Federal Reserve minutes showed persistent inflation concerns and broad support for additional rate increases.[1][3]

items.title: Fed officials discuss potentially larger December rate increase
items.summary: Fed Governor Christopher Waller said policymakers may need to be more aggressive against persistent inflation and suggested a 50-basis-point December increase could be necessary. New York Fed President John Williams also indicated further rate increases could be appropriate if economic conditions evolve as expected.[6][9]

items.title: Nvidia beats estimates but shares fall
items.summary: Nvidia reported quarterly revenue of $115.8 billion and adjusted earnings per share of $2.68, both ahead of expectations, and issued a stronger-than-expected outlook. Shares nevertheless dropped about 2.9% amid investor concerns following co-founder Jensen Huang’s reported departure.[1][8]

items.title: Anthropic prices IPO above target range
items.summary: Anthropic reportedly priced its initial public offering at $83 per share, above its planned $70-$78 range. The offering is described as one of the largest IPOs on record and the first major public listing by a frontier AI-model developer.[1][3]

items.title: Gold and copper slide amid hawkish Fed outlook
items.summary: Gold fell 3.4% to a 14-month low and copper declined 5.25% as hawkish Federal Reserve commentary supported the U.S. dollar and raised expectations for tighter monetary policy.[3]

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin and Ether Extend Slide as Crypto Liquidations Near $2 Billion
items.summary: Bitcoin fell below $64,000, down 1.69% over 24 hours and 13.48% over seven days, while Ether declined 1.89% daily and 12.80% weekly. Roughly $2 billion in leveraged positions were liquidated, primarily long positions.[1]

items.title: World Bank Explores Stablecoin Payments With Circle and Citi
items.summary: The World Bank is examining whether Circle’s USDC and Citi’s payment infrastructure could improve cross-border fund disbursements to developing economies. The initiative remains exploratory, with no launched payment service or disclosed transaction volume.[1]

items.title: CFTC Approves Blockchain-Based Derivatives Platforms
items.summary: The CFTC approved Backpack and tZERO to operate blockchain-based derivatives exchanges and clearinghouses, expanding regulated infrastructure for crypto futures and perpetual products.[3]

items.title: Visa and DBS Expand Institutional Stablecoin Services
items.summary: Visa announced a pilot allowing eligible Asia-Pacific clients to fund Visa Direct cross-border payouts with stablecoins, while DBS and Circle announced direct institutional USDC minting and redemption with round-the-clock settlement.[4]

items.title: LUKSO Exploit Drains 1.4 Million LYX
items.summary: An attacker exploited LUKSO’s email-based recovery backend and took approximately 1.4 million LYX from about 300 Universal Profiles, later swapping the assets for roughly 50 ETH.[4]

items.title: Bitwise Files for Spot Zcash ETF
items.summary: Bitwise filed an S-1 registration statement for a spot Zcash ETF intended to list on the Texas Stock Exchange, potentially adding another regulated investment vehicle for privacy-focused cryptocurrency exposure.[4]

items.title: PancakeSwap Rebrands as Pancake
items.summary: PancakeSwap changed its brand to Pancake as it expands beyond token swaps. The company said the CAKE token remains unchanged and that holders do not need to migrate or claim anything.[4]

items.title: North Korea-Linked Wallets Move $137 Million in Ether
items.summary: A North Korea-linked hacker reportedly dispersed about 74,881 ETH, valued at approximately $137 million, across multiple addresses in activity connected to an earlier Binance hack.[6]

items.title: OSL MENA Receives Preliminary Dubai Broker-Dealer Approval
items.summary: OSL MENA received in-principle approval from Dubai’s VARA for broker-dealer services, a step toward expanding its regulated virtual-asset business in the region.[8]

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: Microsoft unveils new AI models and agent capabilities
items.summary: Microsoft announced several new models, including MAI-Code-2, MAI-Image-2.7 and MAI-Cyber-2-Flash, alongside updates to Foundry for continuously improving AI agents and models. Microsoft-Decision-1.1 also became generally available for routing, classification and workflow-control tasks.

items.title: Google reportedly releases Gemini 4 Neon
items.summary: Google reportedly released Gemini 4 Neon for AI Pro users, positioning it as a lower-cost model for complex tasks. The available report provides limited independent detail about the model’s capabilities.

items.title: OpenAI reportedly launches GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol
items.summary: Several reports say OpenAI launched GPT-6.2 Astra, a flagship reasoning model, and Sol, a faster and cheaper variant, with reduced API pricing for Astra. The claims could not be independently verified from an official OpenAI source in the available results.

items.title: Researchers develop self-editing AI model technique
items.summary: A research report describes a 27-billion-parameter model that can modify internal settings to improve accuracy without conventional retraining. The available source does not provide enough detail to assess the method’s peer-review status or reproducibility.

items.title: AI infrastructure faces water constraints in Gulf region
items.summary: An industry analysis identifies water availability, alongside chips and financing, as a potential constraint on Gulf data-center expansion. It also highlights efforts by major technology companies to develop proprietary models and reduce reliance on external model providers.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Grand Theft Auto VI launches after 13-year wait
items.summary: Rockstar Games’ Grand Theft Auto VI has begun its global rollout, returning players to Vice City on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S. The launch features protagonists Lucia and Jason and is expected to be followed by a PC release next year.[3][10]

items.title: GTA VI launch drives Take-Two shares higher
items.summary: Take-Two Interactive shares rose more than 8% as GTA VI rolled out, reflecting strong market expectations around the franchise’s commercial impact. The game reportedly launched with strong reviews and substantial preorder demand.[8][10]

items.title: The World of Dokkaebi tops mobile-game revenue charts
items.summary: Kakao Games’ 2.5D MMORPG The World of Dokkaebi reached the No. 1 revenue position on both Google Play and Apple’s App Store on November 18. The game also won an Excellence Award at the 2026 Korea Game Awards.[6]

items.title: GTA VI launch creates major gaming frenzy
items.summary: Players and retailers across West Michigan prepared for GTA VI’s release, with demand focused on consoles, controllers and digital downloads. The launch highlights the continued shift away from traditional midnight retail lines toward digital distribution.[2]
